Audit a masque object for leakage and shareability risks

Source: R/audit.R
audit_mask.Rd

Returns a per-column audit data.table, with table-level checks attached, and prints a severity-grouped report. Auto-runs in mode = "collaborate" at mask() time and stores the result on the masque object (m@audit); for local-mode audits or explicit re-audits, pass the original data frame via original.

Usage

audit_mask(m, original = NULL, print = TRUE)

Arguments

m

A masque object from mask(), or a masque_set from mask_set().

original

Optional. Required when m@audit is NULL (typically in local mode). Used to recompute exact-match-pct etc. on demand. The original data frame for a masque; for a masque_set, a named list holding the original table of every table in the set.

print

Logical; if TRUE (default), print a styled report.

Value

The audit data.table, returned invisibly. For a masque_set, a named list of per-table audit data.tables, printed table by table.

Details

Each row of the returned data.table holds:

  • col: column name in the original.

  • role: assigned role.

  • kind: storage kind.

  • leakage_class: low, medium, or high.

  • n_unique_levels: distinct non-NA values (categorical only).

  • freq_min: minimum per-level frequency (categorical only).

  • exact_match_pct: percentage of synthetic cells equal to the original cell (numeric only; cell-by-cell).

  • na_pct: percentage of NA cells in the original column.

  • na_pattern_uniqueness: fraction of rows in the original with a globally unique NA pattern (one number per data frame, repeated on every row).

  • alias_status: aliased, permuted, passthrough, or dropped.

  • notes: short human summary.

  • same_row_pct: percentage of rows where the clone value equals the original value in the same row, read back through the level map (categorical, logical, date and two-valued numeric columns).

  • baseline_pct: the same share expected by chance, under a random permutation of the original column: \(100 \sum_k p_k^2\) over its level frequencies (within the conditioning strata for a scrambled numeric column of a conditional clone).

  • excess_pct: same_row_pct - baseline_pct.

The table-level checks sit in attr(audit, "joint"), a data.table with one row per check (check, cols, observed, baseline, excess, sd, leakage_class, notes). Each baseline comes from independent permutations of the original content columns (outcomes, covariates, dates, kept text), drawn under a fixed internal seed that leaves the caller's random number stream untouched; design, treatment, id, aliased text and linked columns are held fixed:

  • same_row_joint: rows whose every content column equals the original row.

  • whole_row: clone rows equal to some original row on every retained column.

  • rare_cross: in the cross of visible (not aliased) categorical covariates and outcomes, clone cells holding one row whose combination is also a single row in the original.

  • unit_sizes: a note, never graded, when design units differ in size, since the multiset of sizes can link a clone to a public trial list.

Classification heuristics:

  • Retained PII-pattern column -> high.

  • Outcome with action keep in collaborate -> high, or medium when mask() was called with allow_kept_outcome = TRUE, which the recipe records.

  • Treatment unaliased in collaborate -> high. A numeric treatment (a dose) is aliased like a categorical one.

  • Categorical covariate with a frequency-1 level in collaborate -> high.

  • Outcome with exact-match-pct > 1\

  • Numeric covariate with exact-match-pct > 5\ medium.

  • Two-valued numeric columns skip the two exact-match rules: a 0/1 column matches its own cell about half the time by chance. So do columns synthesised once per design unit (see grain in mask()) and whole-valued numeric covariates, which repeat real values by construction; all three are graded on excess_pct instead.

  • Content column whose excess_pct is at least 10 points and four binomial standard deviations in collaborate -> medium.

  • Joint match excess of at least 20 points and four permutation standard deviations -> high (5 points -> medium); rare-cross excess of at least 3 cells and four standard deviations -> high (1 cell and three -> medium). In collaborate mode these verdicts raise masque_high_leakage and block package-managed writers; in local mode they are reported in the notes and graded low.

  • Ignore column retained in local -> low (informational).

A column constant within a design unit that was synthesised row by row (grain = FALSE, or a collaborate grain with fewer than five units) carries a note saying the clone does not keep that grain.

As a reference point, a collaborate-mode clone of agridat::besag.met (yield as the outcome, design columns kept) scores low on every column, and none of its yields equals the original value.

See also

mask().

Examples

r <- propose_roles(iris)
r$role[r$col == "Sepal.Length"] <- "outcome"
r$role[r$col == "Species"] <- "covariate"
m <- mask(iris, r, mode = "collaborate", seed = 1)
#> Re-resolved default actions for mode "collaborate" (explicit edits always win):
#> • Species: scramble -> alias
audit_mask(m)
#> 
#> ── masque audit (mode = collaborate) ───────────────────────────────────────────
#> • 0 HIGH, 0 medium, 5 low across 5 columns
#> • Rows with a globally unique NA pattern: 0.0%
#> 
#> ── LOW (5) ──
#> 
#> ℹ   outcome   Sepal.Length                      ok
#> ℹ   covariate Sepal.Width                       ok
#> ℹ   covariate Petal.Length                      ok
#> ℹ   covariate Petal.Width                       ok
#> ℹ   covariate Species                           levels aliased
#> 
#> ── Table-level checks ──
#> 
#> ℹ   LOW       same-row joint match 0.0% vs chance 0.0% (sd 0.7)
#> ℹ   LOW       whole-row match 0.0% vs chance 0.0% (sd 0.7)
